key_insights: The ten proposed mechanisms collapse to four independent things to build. Mechanisms 1 (FlyHash), 2 (fly Bloom filter), 9 (Spi-Fly) and 10 (SDM) are the same primitive — random expansion, sparsification, read/write on the sparse code — and mechanism 7 only claims to be. Mechanism 3 (Huang 2024 gamma-to-alpha promotion) is a phenomenon whose only runnable formalisation is mechanism 4 (Gkanias incentive circuit), and mechanisms 5 (active forgetting) and 6 (extinction netting) already exist inside mechanism 4 as named roles (the forgetting DAN, the reciprocal-LTM erasure microcircuit). The design phase should build: (a) a sparse-expansion coder, (b) a two-tier store with a readout-triggered promotion gate and a suppressible forgetting daemon, (c) a signed-evidence ledger netted at read, (d) a signed multi-hop graph operator.

MAJOR CORRECTION for the design phase: FlyPrompt (ICLR 2026, the paper the sweep called a 'sparse-expansion router') does NOT use sparse expansion. Its REAR router is a DENSE Gaussian random matrix R_ij ~ N(0,1), M=10,000, followed by ReLU — no sparse binary projection, no winner-take-all, no fan-in constraint, no enforced activity level. It is RanPAC-style random-feature expansion plus a closed-form ridge-regression router, not FlyHash. The paper's own ablation shows the gain comes from expert modularity, not the expansion: RanPAC alone scores 79.92 A_last vs FlyPrompt 86.76 on CIFAR-100. The fly framing is motivation in the abstract, not a constraint on the model. Recommend it on engineering merit (gradient-free, single-pass, closed-form routing suits a growing SKILL.md resolver layer), never on lineage.

Only ONE of the ten mechanisms can be built exactly as published: the fly Bloom filter (PNAS 2018, Eq. 2). Its state is O(m) floats independent of items inserted, it reads novelty before writing, and additive-increase/multiplicative-decay gives eviction for free — the paper explicitly motivates this for 'life-long learning applications, where the database is not of fixed size but continuously grows.' But delta and epsilon are free parameters with no data-derived values (only the AIMD shape is evidenced), the largest n ever tested is 5,000, and it has NEVER been run on text or embeddings. Everything else in the inventory is Analogy or Superficial fidelity.

The Huang 2024 promotion mechanism is the strongest architectural idea and it inverts current practice: consolidation is not a cron job, it is triggered by the hot tier's own readout crossing a threshold. Specifically, STM writing depresses MBON-gamma1pedc>alpha/beta, which weakens its inhibitory feedback onto PPL1-alpha'2alpha2 and PPL1-alpha3; only with that inhibition lifted do those DANs gate LTM formation, after ~3 conditioning bouts. Agent-memory systems do the opposite (agents write, a scheduled librarian later prunes). The untested assumption is that an agent brain has a readout signal playing MBON-gamma1pedc's role — the fly's gate is a two-node circuit fact, not a usage counter.

Two of Tan's five brain-hygiene requirements have NO fly counterpart and never will: provenance on every fact (the mushroom body discards the episode and keeps a scalar synaptic weight — it is a valence tagger, not a document store) and skillification/procedural memory. A third, relevance to a query, is absent from every memory mechanism here: fly promotion, forgetting and arbitration all operate on recency, valence and interference, and none of them knows what a question is. Every one of mechanisms 3-6 needs a relevance term bolted on that is derived from no biology.

The two most immediately usable artifacts are also the two whose biological claim is weakest — and both are actively maintained MIT-licensed code, unlike the genuinely fly-faithful repos which are dormant or unlicensed. connectome_interpreter (35 stars, pip, v2.9.5, benchmarked at ~140k nodes on a laptop) gives signed multi-hop path compression that maps directly onto a supports/contradicts/supersedes document graph — but the operator is just A^n on a column-normalised sparse matrix, a general graph method. Meanwhile InsectRobotics/IncentiveCircuit, the most complete runnable mushroom-body memory model in existence, has 1 star, is GPL-3.0, and was last pushed in 2023.

The clean crux experiment is cheap and nobody has run it: fly Bloom filter (PNAS 2018 Eq. 2 over k-WTA codes computed ON TOP OF dense embeddings, not shingles) versus SAGE's von Mises-Fisher novelty gate, on the same agent-memory benchmark. SAGE already occupies this exact architectural slot with published numbers (3.4x cheaper add-phase, 2.5x lower latency, 16-18% fewer LLM calls as a drop-in gate for A-Mem) and Apache-2.0 code. The fly filter has zero agent-memory benchmarks. H3D never evaluated FlyHash over embeddings — that empty cell is the decisive one and it is cheap to fill.

key_facts.claim: FlyHash is defined by sparse binary projection with expansion m >> d (fly: ~50 projection neurons -> ~2,000 Kenyon cells, ~6 inputs per KC) followed by winner-take-all keeping the top ~5%. Reported gains: MNIST k=4, classical LSH 16.0% mAP -> fly 44.8%; SIFT k=4, WTA vs random tag selection at equal op count 17.7% -> 32.4%. The sparse binary projection gives near-identical performance to dense Gaussian at a factor-of-20 computational saving. Gains are largest at short hash lengths and shrink as k grows.

Fly Bloom filter update rule (PNAS 2018 Eq. 2, read directly from the open CSHL PDF): weights w in [0,1]^m all initialised to 1; for the k active KCs w(i) <- w(i)*delta with 0 <= delta < 1 (multiplicative decay), for the m-k inactive KCs w(i) <- w(i)+epsilon with 0 <= epsilon <= 1 (additive increase); novelty(x) = (1/k) * sum of the k active weights, read BEFORE the write, in [0,1]. Setting delta=epsilon=0 recovers a classical binary Bloom filter exactly. Biological m=350 (of 2,000 KCs read by MBON-alpha'3); experiments used m=30n with a robustness check at m=10n.

Fly Bloom filter results (correlation between ground-truth and predicted novelty, 10-fold CV): fly odours 0.657+/-0.06 vs LSBF 0.537+/-0.08; primate faces 0.508+/-0.03 vs 0.404+/-0.03; SIFT (n=5,000, d=128) 0.535+/-0.03 vs LSBF 0.345+/-0.03 vs traditional Bloom filter 0.002+/-0.02. The paper explicitly states 'there is little biological knowledge of how distance sensitivity and time sensitivity combine' — the combined case appears only in SI Appendix Table S4 as candidate objective functions.

Huang et al. 2024: gamma compartments hold short-term memory with a ~30-min plasticity time constant (MBON-gamma1pedc>alpha/beta depression lasts <1 h); alpha'2alpha2/alpha3 hold long-term memory (~100-min decay for the first ~3 h then far slower; MBON-alpha3 depression persists >24 h). Promotion is gated, not scheduled: STM writing depresses MBON-gamma1pedc>alpha/beta, which weakens its inhibitory feedback onto PPL1-alpha'2alpha2 and PPL1-alpha3; only then do those DANs encode net innate+learnt valence, which gates LTM formation. Requires ~3 conditioning bouts. Evidence: time-lapse in vivo voltage imaging in >500 flies; model is a 9-neuron spiking network across 3 modules (5 DANs, 3 MBONs, 2 KCs, 1 shock neuron) with bidirectional anti-Hebbian plasticity.

Gkanias 2022 dopaminergic plasticity rule: Delta_W_ij(t) = delta_j(t) * [k_i(t) + W_ij(t) - w_rest] with w_rest = 1, yielding four regimes (depression, potentiation, recovery toward rest when KC is inactive and delta<0, saturation). Circuit is 6 MBONs (susceptible/restrained/LTM per valence) and 6 DANs (discharging/charging/forgetting per valence) across five named microcircuits, including MAM in which the forgetting DAN depresses the same-valence restrained MBON — i.e. promotion and STM eviction are one operation. Validated against 92 intervention experiments from 14 studies, r=0.76, p=2.2e-18. Authors' own negative results: fails to reproduce blocking; neglects APL inhibition, KC->KC, KC->DAN, DAN->MBON connections; only 10 KCs for 2 odours; the w_rest term has no known biophysical basis.

FlyPrompt's REAR router uses phi(x) = sigma(hR) with R_ij ~ N(0,1) DENSE Gaussian, M = 10,000, sigma = ReLU, and no top-k or winner-take-all sparsification; the router U is solved in closed form by ridge regression Uhat^T = (G + lambda*I)^-1 * Q. Ablation on CIFAR-100 A_last: full 86.76, minus TE2 84.23, minus REAR 83.75, both removed 73.30, and RanPAC (random projection analytic classifier without expert modularity) 79.92. Code: github.com/AnAppleCore/FlyGCL, MIT, 18 stars, pushed 2026-09-04.

Active forgetting in Drosophila runs on a pathway separable from acquisition at the same synapse: acquisition requires the dDA1 receptor, forgetting requires DAMB (Berry 2012, Neuron 74:530-542, DOI 10.1016/j.neuron.2012.04.007 — note the sweep's cited DOI was wrong); downstream, Scribble scaffolds Rac1->Pak3->cofilin (Cervantes-Sandoval 2016, Neuron 90:1230-1242). Rate is set by the CONTINUOUS ongoing activity of two DANs (MP1, MV1) that fire before and after learning. Increasing sleep drive (Gaboxadol or genetic stimulation of the sleep circuit) decreases that ongoing dopaminergic activity and enhances retention; arousal accelerates forgetting (Berry 2015, Cell 161:1656-1667). Rac inhibition extends early memory from a few hours to >1 day and blocks interference-induced forgetting without affecting acquisition (Shuai 2010, Cell 140:579-589).

Felsenberg 2018: extinction does not erase or overwrite. Omission of expected punishment recruits REWARD dopaminergic neurons and is remembered as a positive experience; the original aversive trace and the new appetitive extinction trace coexist as calcium traces in different places in the MBON network and are integrated on shared avoidance-driving MBONs, where extinction-evoked plasticity neutralises the potentiated response. Paper's own summary: flies 'track the accuracy of learned expectations by accumulating and integrating memories of conflicting events.' Limit: the output is a net valence, never a truth value — no operation returns 'claim A is correct'.

connectome_interpreter's compress_paths takes a column-normalised sparse matrix (each column sums to 1, so entries are proportions of a node's total input) and returns A^0..A^n by chunked repeated sparse matmul; root=True takes the n-th root so path lengths are comparable. compress_paths_signed splits each step into excitatory and inhibitory streams via a per-neuron +1/-1 sign map, treating an even number of inhibitions as excitation. Documented caveats: column sums fall below 1 where nodes have no upstream partners, truncating paths; raw values shrink monotonically with n. MIT licence, 35 stars, pip install connectome-interpreter v2.9.5, pushed 2026-08-27, benchmarked at ~140,000 nodes on a laptop. Preprint: Yin, Hoeller, Mathiasen, Tsang, Charrier & Cardona, bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.09.29.679410.

Spi-Fly is a [72-1000-10] / [5-1000-18] spiking network with fixed sparse random PN->KC connectivity (~20% connection probability, ~10x expansion), winner-take-all leaving ~5% of hidden units active, and learning confined to hidden->output weights by a local supervised Hebbian rule. Gas-sensor dataset: 88.8% after 1 epoch (3 presentations per odour) vs BPTT 56.3%; class-incremental, Spi-Fly holds ~88% while BPTT collapses to near chance and EWC+BPTT shows 'no significant improvement'. Negative results: BPTT overtakes it with more training (83.9% vs 58.9% on the synthetic set after 10 epochs); no input->hidden learning; needs labels; single odours only, no mixtures; ignores spike timing. Code claimed at Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18786636 — could NOT be resolved at check time (HTTP 504 on both DOI redirect and API).

The most usable open implementation of the fly Bloom filter as an ingest/dedup gate is clembarr/ffbf-novelty-detector (Rust core + Python bindings, add()/tick() API, ~4.7 KiB state at m=1200, README explicitly targets 'drop near-duplicates before an expensive stage (embedding, indexing, an LLM call)' and cache admission). It has 0 stars, NO LICENSE FILE (not legally reusable), no benchmarks, no identified author, and was first pushed 2026-09-08 — two days before this report. Treat as reference reading, not a dependency; PNAS Eq. 2 is ~20 lines to reimplement.

Xie & Ocker 2025 (correct title: 'The Impact of Structural Changes on Learning Capacity in the Fly Olfactory Neural Circuit') is the direct negative result against aggressive pruning: random and targeted pruning of KC->MBON synapses degrades odour classification much as ablation does, MBONs with very few presynaptic KCs consistently perform worst, and ablating developmentally MATURE Kenyon cells hurts more than ablating immature ones — i.e. 'prune the old stuff' is the wrong default for a well-established index.

Bricken & Pehlevan show transformer attention approximates Kanerva's Sparse Distributed Memory read under a binomial approximation to the address distance distribution, with an explicit Hamming-radius r <-> softmax beta correspondence verified to hold in pretrained GPT-2. The actionable follow-up (Bricken, Davies, Singh, Krotov, Kreiman, ICLR 2023, arXiv:2303.11934) is that an MLP with Top-K activation, L2 normalisation and positive weight constraints is a strong continual learner with no replay, no task information and no task boundaries, and every one of those three biological components is necessary. Caveat for question (b): SDM is the same sparse-expansive-code motif reached independently by Kanerva in 1988, which strengthens the general claim and weakens the specifically-fly one. Both repos are dormant and SDMContinualLearner has no licence.

Report written to /Users/stephen/Cookies/company-brain-research/findings/g07-neuro-mechanism-inventory.md (437 lines): all ten mechanisms with one-paragraph algorithms (inputs/outputs/parameters), primary-source citations verified directly against papers and repos, negative results, and deep/analogy/superficial fidelity ratings.

For the design phase (d1-d5), three things should change how the specs get written.

FIRST, propagate the FlyPrompt correction before anyone builds on it. The sweep's line "sparse-expansion router for the RESOLVER/skill layer (FlyPrompt)" is factually wrong about the algorithm: REAR is a dense Gaussian matrix with ReLU (M=10,000) and closed-form ridge regression, with no sparse binary projection and no winner-take-all. The paper's own ablation shows the gain comes from expert modularity, not expansion (RanPAC 79.92 vs FlyPrompt 86.76). Keep FlyGCL as a recommendation on engineering merit — it is the best-maintained repo in the inventory and gradient-free single-pass routing genuinely suits a growing skill layer — but strip the fly attribution. Checkpoints/01-sweep-decisions.md item (iii) needs the same edit that v10a asked for on item (b).

SECOND, build the crux experiment around mechanism 2, not mechanism 1. Only the fly Bloom filter can be built exactly as published, and the missing cell in the literature is precise and cheap: k-WTA codes computed on top of dense embeddings (Dasgupta's actual m >> d regime, ~5% activity) rather than over shingles, feeding the PNAS Eq. 2 AIMD novelty score, benchmarked against SAGE's von Mises-Fisher gate on the same agent-memory task. SAGE occupies that architectural slot today with published cost/latency numbers and Apache-2.0 code; the fly filter has none. Kill criterion writes itself: if the fly gate does not match SAGE's write-reduction at equal downstream F1, the write-side fly bridge is dead and only mechanism 8 survives.

THIRD, be honest in the synthesis about which half of each recommendation is biology. Two artifacts do real work — connectome_interpreter (signed multi-hop compression, MIT, laptop-scale at 140k nodes) and FlyGCL — and both have weak biological claims. The genuinely fly-faithful code is dormant or unlicensed: IncentiveCircuit has 1 star and GPL-3.0, ffbf-novelty-detector has no licence and is two days old, SDMContinualLearner has no licence. The strongest *idea* in the inventory (Huang 2024's readout-gated promotion — consolidation triggered by the hot tier's own signal rather than a cron job) has no implementation at all and rests on an untested assumption that an agent-side analogue of MBON-gamma1pedc's disinhibition exists. And provenance, skillification, and relevance-to-a-query have no fly counterpart whatsoever, so the design must state plainly that fly mechanisms cover the write gate, the tiering trigger, and the forgetting daemon — never the content store.

designs.recommendation: Build `flygate`: a stateful scoring seam on GBrain's write path, inserted immediately after the existing exact-`content_hash` dedup pre-check at `src/core/import-file.ts:756` and before chunking, that computes TWO fly Bloom filter novelty scores (PNAS 2018 Eq. 2, built exactly as published) over one shared FlyHash code of the page's head-slice embedding — a fast compartment with a ~4-day memory and a slow one with a ~25-day memory, mirroring the mushroom body's gamma and alpha compartments reading the same Kenyon cells. Two filters are not decoration: a single (delta, epsilon) pair yields one horizon, and I derive that one duplicate insert is worth exactly H_min = m/(k*r) days of drift, so a month-long clock necessarily compresses its duplicate signal to ~7% of the readout range. Two time constants over one code separate distance from time — a direct answer to PNAS 2018's own stated open problem — and quantise into three write-time routes: chronic duplicate (skip the `synthesize` triage judge at cycle/synthesize.ts:129 and skip `takes` extraction, saving $0.0128/page), genuinely novel (admit unexamined), and the band that justifies the whole design, RECURRENCE AFTER DORMANCY — content similar to something the brain saw three weeks ago but not this week, which is exactly where superseded facts live and which GBrain's probe structurally cannot see, because it is query-sampled and its pipeline literally reads "Date pre-filter: skip pairs whose dates are >30d apart". Judging only that band at write time, with the source still in context, costs ~$0.68/month at 250 writes/day against a ~$96/month curation line, and breaks even if it suppresses 0.7% of writes. Total build: 11 engineering days, ~$150 of eval spend, 1.05 MB of state per source, +4-6 ms p99 (the lazy-update form makes read and write O(k) rather than O(m)). Ship it default-OFF with four pluggable scorers and default `scorer: hybrid` — because I concede plainly that SimHash owns near-duplicate dedup (it beats FlyHash on both H3D datasets on quality AND time), `1 - max cosine` from one free HNSW probe owns the distance axis, a SQL query on the already-indexed `pages.last_retrieved_at` owns the long horizon, and SQL:2011 `PRIMARY KEY (key, period WITHOUT OVERLAPS)` is a strictly better answer to arbitration than any novelty score. The fly owns exactly one unoccupied cell: content-level recurrence after dormancy. Run kill criterion K2 in week one on offline vectors with no GBrain code touched — if the two-filter readout cannot beat every time-blind baseline by >=10 points AUROC on a recurrence corpus, the entire fly branch is closed for four days and ~$0, and the seam ships with the boring scorer. My confidence the fly wins that test is ~40%; my confidence the SEAM is worth building regardless is high, and that distinction is the honest deliverable.

Replace GBrain's promotion TRIGGER, not its store. Today `consolidate` promotes facts to takes only when the same thing was said three times in near-identical words (`HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3` plus a cosine-0.85 cluster of size >= 2), and the measured result on a live store was 62 buckets processed and zero facts promoted (gbrain#3042); meanwhile forgetting is a pure read-time sort function that never writes back, and the only automatic arbitration rule is recency-inside-a-cosine-cluster. Borrow three things from the mushroom body, all Analogy-fidelity, all deterministic, all zero-LLM by default. (L1) Readout-gated promotion, after Huang et al. 2024: promote when the hot tier has been both written to (E=2) and READ BACK on B=3 spaced bouts, which lets singleton facts promote and is a five-line change to `consolidate.ts` behind a `lifecycle.promotion_gate` enum defaulting to today's behaviour; the readout signal already exists in `src/core/last-retrieved.ts`, is deliberately op-layer-only ("a user-facing surface just surfaced this page"), already has a 5-minute refractory throttle, and is currently spent on an idea GENERATOR — and I verified that adding a bout counter cannot invalidate the query cache because `bump_page_generation_fn()` uses a column allow-list that excludes it. (L2) A forgetting daemon that is separately parameterised, continuously running, and suppressible (Berry 2012/2015, Shuai 2010, Cervantes-Sandoval 2016), which DEMOTES rather than deletes — suppression multiplied into `effectiveConfidence`, reset on any recall, budget slaved to the acquisition rate per CREW's rate law, suppressed while an `open_loops` row is active or the contradiction judge is failing — because Xie & Ocker show pruning a fly index degrades it, GBrain's one at-scale automatic deletion was a silent 324-fact accident, and its D17 doctrine refuses semantic mutation on principle. (L3) Extinction-as-accumulation for conflicting takes (Felsenberg 2018): a `claim_evidence` ledger of signed events with SEPARATELY parameterised decay per compartment, netted at read and always returned WITH the ledger, whose signs come free from the existing `eval_contradictions_cache` verdicts — this is not an arbiter (v09b shows hand-written rules lose to LLM judges on real conflicting sources) but the escape hatch for g01's SQL:2011 `WITHOUT OVERLAPS` constraint, i.e. the implementation of the "debate" state g01 says GBrain cannot currently mint. Total marginal cost $0-$11/month and ~15.5 engineer-days. Be honest about what this is: every component has a non-biological incumbent that is at least as good (W-TinyLFU admission, CREW retention schedules, SQL:2011 bitemporal), so the experiment includes a fly-free control arm (B5) and a pre-registered BIOLOGY kill criterion — if B5 ties within 1 pp, publish that the fruit-fly framing added nothing. And run kill criterion K5 first, on day zero, before writing any code: compute the AUROC of the readout signal for predicting "cited in a correct answer" on 30 days of existing `last_retrieved_at` history; below 0.60 the whole promotion redesign dies for one day of work and no LLM spend, which is exactly the untested assumption g07 flagged as load-bearing. Predicted headline outcome, stated in advance: a pooled null (+0 to +3 pp on n=3,024), with the real effect confined to MemConflict static+conditional (+4 to +10 pp on n=804), superseded-serving rate (-8 to -20 pp), and cold-tier yield (a literal zero today).

Retire the fly router and ship the boring one, but keep the fly gate as a separately-killable experiment. I ran the assigned angle before proposing it: on GBrain's own 73 skills and 271 routing fixtures, FlyPrompt's REAR expansion and a true FlyHash k-WTA router both lose to a no-training nearest-centroid retriever at every pool size in the trigger-blind condition (REAR -1.1 pp, FlyHash -1.4 to -5.9 pp at pool 73, with regularisation swept in the expansion arms' favour), so checkpoint decision (iii) should be struck and the fly hash has now lost its third socket after index and dedup. What the exercise found instead is worth building: GBrain's shipped router is a substring matcher scoring 303/303 = 100% on fixtures that collapse to 0/271 = 0% when you delete only the phrases each intent literally copies; its declared generalisation layer ("Layer B (LLM tie-break)... Not yet implemented in this release") is an empty slot; no skill is embedded anywhere in the repo; its one real routing A/B inverts under exact-slug scoring (compression 63/60/53 vs baseline 82/87/73 STRICT); and the always-on skill manifest costs $528-$1,077/month uncached at 150-306 skills for a 25-person company, against g02's ~$225/month for the entire brain. So: implement Layer B as a two-stage dispatcher -- stage 1 dense nearest-prototype retrieval over skill descriptions (RAG-MCP, arXiv:2505.03275, explicitly non-biological), stage 2 a fly Bloom filter (Dasgupta PNAS 2018, the only Deep-fidelity mechanism in g07's inventory) computing abstention and routing-drift, shipped in `shadow` mode, stage 3 LLM escalation only on low margin. Insertion points are concrete: src/core/routing-eval.ts Layer B, a new src/core/skill-router.ts, a derived skill_prototypes table on the existing pgvector index, a route_prototypes phase after embed in cycle.ts, and decisions written back as `facts` rows so the 7-day event half-life and the dream-consolidate bridge turn trigger maintenance into a measured loop. Do not build a FlyHash/BioHash `vector.backend`, and treat the question as settled rather than open. I specified the proposal at implementation grain against GBrain's real, unbuilt seam (`docs/designs/VECTOR_BACKENDS.md`, `src/core/vector-index.ts:25/33/63/186`, `src/schema.sql:302/336`), pre-registered a three-part kill criterion, then ran the experiment this corpus repeatedly flags as never run by anyone: FlyHash and a trained BioHash computed on top of real dense text embeddings (bge-m3, 1024-d, GBrain's default width; 3,187 chunks cut with GBrain's own 300/50-word chunker), scored against `binary_quantize()` on the same embeddings, in a live pgvector 0.8.6 instance. All three criteria failed on all ~50 swept configurations: at equal storage sign binarization beats FlyHash by +53% relative recall@10 (0.7577 vs 0.4948) and +15.8 points after exact rescoring (0.9918 vs 0.8339); in-database the FlyHash column costs 2.4x the bytes and 2.2x the latency of a `bit(1024)` column and is slower than the float32 vector it was meant to accelerate; and the only FlyHash setting that reaches parity is refused outright with `ERROR: sparsevec cannot have more than 1000 non-zero elements for hnsw index`, so the backend pitched as lifting pgvector's dimension cap in fact introduces a tighter one. Three things survive and belong in the synthesis. First, the fly literature is vindicated on its own axis: at equal *hash length* FlyHash beats random-hyperplane LSH by +82% relative on real text embeddings, apparently the first demonstration on modern encoders — the loss is a resource-accounting inversion (64 indices into m=20,480 is ~960 bits, not 64), so every citation of "16.0% -> 44.8% mAP" must carry "at equal hash length". Second, the non-biological alternative wins on every steelman property the fly proposal claimed — data-independent, training-free, streaming, and lifting the cap to 64,000 dims — so I ship D4-ALT (`vector.backend = pgvector-bq`, complete DDL, ~3-5 dev-days, 22.5x smaller and 1.9x faster at 99.2% recall, worth a Supabase 2XL dropping to a Large at the million-page tier), while stating honestly that it is a hosting-tier win and not a quality win, because g02's arithmetic caps any index victory at 0.14% of an answered question. Third, my near-duplicate measurement corrects v10b and *raises* the bar for the one surviving fly idea: lexical 64-bit SimHash is not the dedup incumbent — it scores 0.263 on paraphrase-shaped edits — the real competitor to a write-side fly gate is the free ANN probe you already paid for (0.843) or its 136-byte binarized shadow (0.834), which d1/d2 must now beat.

Every algorithmic bridge from the fly to a company brain has now been measured and most have failed — FlyHash loses to dense embeddings and even to SimHash, the connectome-topology advantage vanishes under a degree-preserving null, and the one mechanism buildable as published (the fly Bloom filter) has never been run on text. What survives is not in the fly's brain; it is in the filing cabinet of the labs that mapped it. The connectome consortia spent a decade solving, at 166,700 entities and 1.8 billion annotations, exactly the problem Tan says is the product: keeping a corpus worth retrieving from while it is being rewritten underneath you. They solved it with four invariants a company brain can adopt in two weeks — bind every fact to an IMMUTABLE anchor and resolve the mutable entity identity through a LINEAGE GRAPH at a timestamp (CAVE's one genuinely unsubstitutable idea, and the precondition for g01's WITHOUT OVERLAPS constraint, which today would enforce uniqueness on a string the nightly cycle itself rewrites); cut MATERIALISED VERSIONS so a question can be asked as of a date, at a measured 1.9-2.6x latency (525 vs 978 vs 1,385 ms) that is under 10% of GBrain's search budget; carry CONFIDENCE WITH ITS SCALE AND PRODUCER, never normalised across sources and never hidden, with verified beating predicted; and publish a DEPRECATION POLICY in which source-death and fact-death are independent axes, deprecation never deletes, and deprecated items drop out of the denominators as well as the results. Add flyem-snapshot's two-tier curation-status vocabulary whose publish mapping is guarded by a build-breaking assertion, a `gbrain release` that ships its own status-distribution report and a defined denominator (which makes v05's five-conflicting-page-counts problem arithmetically impossible), a queryable map of the corpus's known defects, match_mode and as_of as additive fields on the frozen MEMORY_VERBS surface, and the single evidence-backed behavioural correction: ConnectomeBench says models score 75-85% on split errors and 52-82% on identification but fail on merges, so stop letting the nightly cycle merge pages and start letting it split them. Total cost is zero LLM tokens per page (against a baseline where write-side curation is 222-4,514x embedding spend), roughly +$10-40/month of snapshot storage, and ten engineer-days to an MVP whose first two days are measurement against a kill criterion. Three caveats must travel with it: this is process transfer, not neuroscience, and the synthesis must say so in the same breath; almost every piece has a better-specified standard behind it (W3C Web Annotation, SQL:2011, OBO Foundry, PROV-O, LakeFS) and the connectome earns its place only because it is the one place all of them run together at scale with published costs (~$500/month, 4M edits, 500 users, ~44 person-years); and the modal expected outcome, pre-registered as kill criterion K4, is that this buys reproducibility, arbitrability and governance while moving pooled retrieval accuracy by nothing at all.

METR's RCT found early-2025 AI made 16 experienced open-source developers 19% slower (CI +2% to +39%) while they believed they were 20% faster; its May-2026 survey of 349 technical workers found a median self-reported 1.4-2x value gain - both far below Tan's '8X at the floor'.

GBrain's contradiction probe applies a 'Date pre-filter: skip pairs whose dates are >30d apart', which structurally excludes most real supersessions on a quarterly organisational clock - the one gap the fly Bloom filter's recurrence-after-dormancy band would reach.

MemConflict's released set (Data/Step4_4.jsonl, 39.7 MB) contains 30 instances and 3,750 questions at 202K mean dialogue tokens, split dynamic 2,946 / conditional 444 / static 360; the 804 static+conditional questions are where newest-wins is inverted or undefined and cost ~$30 to run.

SQL:2011 standardised bitemporal tables with PRIMARY KEY (key, period WITHOUT OVERLAPS), shipping in Db2, MariaDB, XTDB and Oracle - the constraint that makes two contradictory live facts unrepresentable at write time. Zep/Graphiti, GBrain and every system surveyed store the timestamps and enforce nothing; GBrain is uni-temporal with an audit stamp, not bi-temporal.

It is the single cheapest experiment that can falsify or confirm the entire "curation beats retrieval" thesis, and every other recommendation in the document is downstream of its answer.
